Name: whole_bank_confusability_ladder
Title: Confusable, Not Long: The Whole-Bank-in-Context Route Loses to Top-k Retrieval Only as Near-Miss Trajectories Accumulate
Short Hypothesis: On a six-procedure trajectory bank read by Qwen3-32B, the whole bank as a cached static prefix matches goal-sentence top-3 retrieval on task success up to the 16k context no matter how many redundant or off-domain items are added, and falls behind only as the count of near-miss items (same object and receptacle words, different procedure) grows. Retrieval is hurt by near-miss items too, but its exposure is capped at k items whose cross-type share equals the bank's share, so at fixed share it is flat in count. At matched length, composition therefore costs the whole-bank route more than retrieval; this route x composition interaction replicates on an independent bank draw and is larger for the weaker reader (Qwen3-8B) on the same size grid, so the bank size at which the routes cross is set by composition and reader, not prompt length.
Related Work: Enrich-Retrieve-Rank (arxiv:2608.22695) shows in-context routing over a capability registry collapsing as the registry grows while retrieve-then-rank degrades gracefully, but scores Match@1 with one router model and grows the number of distinct options, not the number of confusable copies. Bertsch et al. (arxiv:2405.00200) and arxiv:2412.16926 find that long-context ICL gains come from attention to the similar examples and that selection matters less as shots grow, on classification tasks; MANYICLBENCH (arxiv:2411.07130) separates similar-sample from all-sample learning; arxiv:2510.16809 finds a few well-chosen examples beating many on code translation. arxiv:2607.26497 measures a corpus-size crossover between agentic search and BM25 on documents with one reader; arxiv:2603.04814 measures Mem0 against long context on conversational QA with one model; arxiv:2411.05000 shows effective context shorter than advertised on synthetic threads. The compliance trap (arxiv:2607.10608) shows agents adopting conflicting retrieved memory; SkillEvolBench (arxiv:2605.24117) reports clutter from larger libraries under an unspecified selection. None of these grows a trajectory bank while holding the procedure count fixed and separating redundant count, off-domain length and confusable count, scores task success, and checks whether the crossover moves with the reader.
Abstract: Agent-memory papers assume a bank of trajectories must be queried because the whole bank will not fit or will not be read well, and the long-context literature reports crossovers between retrieval and in-context reading measured on documents with one reader. We ask what property of a trajectory bank actually makes the whole-bank-in-context route fall behind top-k retrieval on task success. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B we grow a six-item seed bank (one expert exemplar per task type) to 12-80 items in three ways that hold the six procedures fixed: redundant growth (same-type items whose object-receptacle combos collide with no other type), off-domain filler (token-matched trajectories from another text game), and near-miss growth (every added item has a twin of another type with the same object and receptacle, so half the bank is confusable). Each bank is read whole as a cached static prefix or through goal-sentence top-3 retrieval, on the same 274 games and two seeds, with the Measurement C static arms as the baseline, a type-conditioned retrieval arm and logged top-3 composition to show that retrieved twins are actually adopted rather than merely present, a fixed uniformly random 80-item subset as the selection control, and an independent second bank draw on which the route x composition interaction is confirmed. We predict the whole-bank route is flat under redundant and filler growth and declines with the near-miss count, while retrieval is hurt by twins but flat in count at fixed share, so at matched length composition costs the whole-bank route more than retrieval, and more so for Qwen3-8B on the same size grid. Prefill tokens and GPU-seconds under prefix caching are logged for accuracy-cost curves.
Experiments:
- Bank construction from the expert pool (1,465 items). Seed S6 = one expert exemplar per task type, fixed. Growth rules that keep six procedures: R (redundant, near-miss share 0; sizes 12/48/80): add same-type items whose (object, receptacle) combo appears in no item of another type in the bank. N (near-miss, share 0.5; sizes 12/24/48/80): add items in cross-type twin pairs (same object and receptacle, different procedure; twins chosen so their first actions coincide), so at every size half the items have a twin in the bank; combos sampled from the pool's combo distribution. F (filler, size 80): S6 plus token-matched trajectories from public TextWorld cooking games in the same format with no ALFWorld nouns. U: one uniformly random fixed 80-subset of the pool (natural near-miss share measured and reported) as the G17 fixed-random-selection control. Replicate draw: a second N'-80 and R'-80 built by the same rules from disjoint items and disjoint twin combos with a fresh type-interleaved order. Per bank and size the coverage fraction (share of the 274 test goals whose combo has a twin pair in the bank) is logged. Item order type-interleaved, fixed per arm.
- Routes. WB: whole bank as a type-agnostic static prefix (vLLM prefix caching on, cache hit ratio logged). RET: goal-sentence top-3 from the same bank per episode (uncached), same retriever as Measurement A; per episode the top-3 type composition is logged (cross-type-in-top-3 rate = any item of another type in the top-3; strict twin rate = an item with the goal's object and receptacle and another type). RET-T: top-3 restricted to items of the goal's template type (type-conditioned by construction, reported under the type-conditioning rule), on N-48 only. RET-rand: three random items from the same bank, fixed per game, on N-48 only. All arms run the same 274 games x 2 seeds.
- Arms at Qwen3-32B (23): WB S6; WB R-12/48/80; WB N-12/24/48/80; RET R-12/48/80; RET N-12/24/48/80; RET-T N-48; RET-rand N-48; WB F-80; WB U-80; replicate WB N'-80, WB R'-80, RET N'-80, RET R'-80. The static baselines k0, static3, instr_all, blind1 and RET k=3 on the full pool are Measurement A/C cells on disk, paired on the same games and seeds.
- Reader manipulation (G16) at Qwen3-8B (12 arms): WB and RET on N-12/24/48/80 (the same grid as 32B), WB and RET on R-80, k0 and static3. Precondition run first: 8B static3 minus k0 must exceed +8 net; if it does not, Qwen3-14B replaces 8B as the weaker reader with the same 12 arms, decided before any ladder cell of the weaker reader is run; the reader arm is never reported as uninformative.
- Error signature: in failed episodes, the fraction whose executed action sequence follows a twin procedure (skipped or inserted clean/heat/cool step), read from the action log per route, size and reader; WB success is also split by covered vs uncovered goals per size.
- Cost: GPU-seconds per episode at fixed concurrency (16 workers per replica), prefill tokens per episode, cache hit ratio; accuracy-cost curves per route and size; the cost crossover is reported separately from the accuracy contrasts.
- Budget arithmetic: 23 arms x 548 episodes = 12,604 episodes at 32B; the 8 WB arms at 48/80 items run 2-3x slower per episode (about 2.5 GPU-h each) and the other 15 about 1 GPU-h each, about 35 GPU-h, i.e. about 17.5 h wall on the two A100s with one vLLM replica per GPU and slow WB arms interleaved with RET arms on each replica; 12 arms x 548 = 6,576 episodes at 8B at roughly a third of the per-episode cost, about 6 GPU-h, 3 h wall. Total about 20 h.
- Order: pre-registration (the positive control is already met on Measurement C: the wrong-type placebo blind1 sits 15.4 net below static3); R and N ladders at 32B; RET-T, RET-rand, F, U; replicate draw; then the weaker reader.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Static baselines (Measurement C, on disk, same games and seeds): k0; static3 (best static arm, +12.4 over k0); instr_all (type-agnostic six-procedure prompt); blind1 (wrong-type fixed exemplar: length placebo and near-miss positive control, 15.4 net below static3 and 3 below k0). Every WB and RET cell is reported minus static3 and minus instr_all at its stated tokens; WB at S6 is itself the smallest whole-bank static arm.
- RET k=3 over the natural pool (Measurement A, +17.2 over static3) and RET-rand on N-48 (three random items from the same bank, fixed per game) at the same token budget, to separate the retriever from the exemplar budget.
- RET-T on N-48: type-conditioned retrieval over the same near-miss bank; isolates twin retrieval from item identity (N items are selected for having twins, so N and R banks differ in which expert items they contain).
- WB F-80 isolates prompt length from content; WB U-80 is the matched-budget random-selection control at the whole-context budget and supplies a third, natural near-miss share.
- Replicate bank draw (N'-80, R'-80, both routes) gives the confirmatory interaction cells and absorbs item-identity and order variation between draws.
- Reader ablation: the weaker reader on the full N ladder and at R-80, plus its own k0 and static3.
Falsifiable Predictions:
All contrasts are paired net differences over 274 x 2 with one threshold, 9 net: a decline is confirmed at or below -9 and falsified above it; flatness is confirmed inside +/-9 and falsified at or beyond it.
- P1 (length and redundancy do not hurt the whole-bank route): WB(R-80) - WB(S6) and WB(F-80) - WB(S6) are both within +/-9. Falsified if either is at or below -9 (plain long-context degradation of an 80-item prefix); arms: WB R-80 and WB F-80 against WB S6.
- P2 (confusable count hurts the whole-bank route): at matched length WB(N-80) - WB(R-80) is at or below -9, WB declines monotonically over N-12/24/48/80, and the twin-procedure fraction among WB failures rises by at least 10 points from N-12 to N-80. Falsified if WB(N-80) - WB(R-80) is above -9, or if the decline is not accompanied by the error-signature rise (a generic length or attention failure). Reachable: blind1 costs only 3 net against k0 on Measurement C, so a 32B reader that disambiguates by the goal sentence leaves WB(N-80) flat; arms: WB N-80, WB R-80, WB N-12.
- P3 (retrieved twins are exposed and adopted; retrieval exposure is share-bound, not count-bound): (a) on N-48 the logged cross-type-in-top-3 rate is at least 0.4 (and at most 0.15 on R-48), RET(N-48) - RET(R-48) is at or below -9, and RET-T(N-48) - RET(R-48) is within +/-9. Falsified if the retriever does not expose twins (rate below 0.4 on N-48), if the reader ignores exposed twins (rate reached yet RET(N-48) - RET(R-48) above -9, reachable because a wrong-type item beside a right-type one may be disambiguated as blind1 nearly is against k0), or if RET-T(N-48) stays at or below -9 against RET(R-48) (the N-bank penalty is item identity, not twins). (b) at fixed share RET(N-80) - RET(N-12) is within +/-9, with the cross-type-in-top-3 rate reported per size. Falsified if RET(N-80) - RET(N-12) is at or below -9 (retrieval declines with count, for instance because twin coverage of test goals grows with the number of pairs). Arms: RET N-48, RET R-48, RET-T N-48, RET N-12, RET N-80.
- P4 (headline; route x composition interaction at matched length, confirmed on the replicate draw): [WB(N'-80) - WB(R'-80)] - [RET(N'-80) - RET(R'-80)] is at or below -9 with the paired-bootstrap 90% CI over games excluding 0; the same contrast on the primary draw is reported alongside as exploratory. Falsified if the replicate interaction is above -9 (both routes lose the same to twins, reachable because P3(a) predicts retrieval is hurt too, or whole-bank reading absorbs twins as well as retrieval does) or if the two draws disagree in sign. Arms: WB N'-80, WB R'-80, RET N'-80, RET R'-80, used by no other prediction.
- P5 (the weaker reader is more count-sensitive): with D_reader = [WB - RET](N-80) - [WB - RET](N-12) paired per (game, seed) on the same grid, D_8B - D_32B is at or below -9 with the paired-bootstrap 90% CI excluding 0. Descriptively, the crossing size per reader (where WB - RET fitted against log2 size over 12/24/48/80 crosses -9) is reported with its bootstrap CI, censored at above 80. Falsified if D_8B - D_32B is above -9 (the weaker reader is no more count-sensitive, or is hurt equally on both routes). Both readers run the same 12/24/48/80 grid; the weaker reader's floor check is a precondition with a pre-named fallback, so no outcome is reported as uninformative. Arms: weaker-reader WB/RET N-12/24/48/80 against the 32B cells.
- P6 (fixed random whole bank against the measured natural-pool residual): WB(U-80) - static3 is within +/-9 of the measured k3 - static3 residual (+17.2, CI half-width about 5), i.e. WB(U-80) - k3 within +/-9. Falsified if WB(U-80) - k3 is at or below -9 (a random whole-bank subset loses at least half the retrieval residual) or at or above +9 (the whole bank beats retrieval); the measured natural near-miss count of U-80 places it on the N ladder's count axis, and a loss larger than the ladder predicts at that count also counts against P2's count law. Arm: WB U-80 against Measurement A k=3 and static3.
Measurement and Noise Control: All arms run the same 274 games (140 valid_seen + 134 valid_unseen) x 2 seeds with identical seeds across arms; every contrast is a paired net difference in task-success points. One threshold, 9 net, serves every prediction (decline confirmed at or below -9, flatness confirmed inside +/-9), so there is no dead band between the +/-8 floor at 274 x 2 and the confirmatory margin; 9 net is one third of the Gate-0 k=3 gain over k0 (+27) and about half the measured k3 - static3 residual (+17.2, CI half-width about 5). Every WB and RET cell is also reported minus static3 and minus instr_all on the same (game, seed). Interaction and reader contrasts carry paired-bootstrap 90% CIs resampling games with both seeds moving together; the crossing size is fitted per reader from WB - RET against log2 size on the four shared N sizes with a bootstrap CI, censored at above 80, and is descriptive only. The positive control is already met on Measurement C: blind1 is 15.4 net below static3 and 3 net below k0, so a wrong-type item costs against the right one and barely at all against nothing, which is exactly what makes the reader-disambiguation falsifiers of P2 and P3 reachable. Twin exposure is measured, not assumed: cross-type-in-top-3 and strict twin rates per RET cell, coverage fraction per bank, WB success split by covered vs uncovered goals. Item-identity and order effects are bounded by the replicate draw (different items, combos and interleave) and by RET-T, which holds the bank fixed while removing twin retrieval. Per-type claims are made only on the pooled twin-bearing types (clean, heat, cool, pick-and-place) and declared exploratory. Cost is measured, not modelled: GPU-seconds per episode at fixed concurrency with prefix caching on, prefill tokens and cache hit ratio per episode, reported as accuracy-cost curves. The weaker reader's floor check (static3 - k0 above +8) is a precondition with Qwen3-14B as the pre-named fallback; the reader arm is never reported as uninformative. Pre-registration before the first ladder cell.

Risk Factors and Limitations:
- Near-miss harm may be small for a 32B reader because the goal sentence disambiguates the type (blind1 costs only 3 net against k0); that is the falsifying outcome of P2 and P3, not a design risk, and is reported as such.
- N and R banks contain different expert items because N items are selected for having twins; RET-T and the replicate draw bound this for retrieval and across draws, but no whole-bank analogue with twins' types relabelled exists, so a WB-only identity effect would appear as P2 confirmed with P4 falsified.
- Twin coverage of the 274 test goals grows with the number of pairs, so on the N ladder a count effect and a coverage effect are entangled; the covered/uncovered split and the logged coverage fraction separate them descriptively, not by manipulation.
- Only six procedures exist on ALFWorld, so the registry-growth regime of 2608.22695 (hundreds of distinct options) is not reachable here; the claim is limited to fixed-procedure banks, with WebShop as the stated extension.
- Twins are scarce for look-at-in-light and pick-two, so the N ladder's twin-bearing types are clean, heat, cool and pick-and-place; per-type results outside these are exploratory.
- 16k context caps the ladder at 80 items; a 32k extension on this node would cut concurrency and is not proposed.
- Whole-bank arms at 48/80 items run 2-3x slower per episode; the budget accounts for this and throughput is reported per arm.
- Qwen3-8B may be near its k=0 floor on ALFWorld; the precondition and the Qwen3-14B fallback keep P5 decidable, at the cost that the reader gap may be smaller than planned.
Addresses gap: G19 (primary): saturation with the number of shots and whether a whole-bank prompt matches retrieval past saturation, here with the bank composition manipulated rather than observed; also G17 (matched-budget whole-bank and fixed-random-selection arms) and G16 (crossover measured with two readers on the same size grid).
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: Measurement A ('unseen ~ seen, so the retrieved value is the type's procedure; a bank of 1,465 items has at most six procedures') observes the natural pool; this idea builds banks whose redundant, off-domain and confusable item counts are set separately and claims the whole-bank route's success tracks the confusable count only, with retrieval's exposure capped at k, which Measurement A cannot say. Nearest digest card: arxiv:2608.22695 observes routing collapse with registry size on Match@1 with one router; this idea claims that on trajectory banks with a fixed procedure count collapse does not come with size at all but with near-miss items, scored on task success with two readers, and shows by logged top-3 composition and a type-conditioned retrieval arm that retrieved twins are adopted rather than merely present. Nearest archived ideas: coverage_limited_context_count_limited_weights (5.35) claims context is coverage-limited; this idea claims what governs the route past coverage (confusable count vs length), which it neither manipulated nor measured; compile_dont_retrieve and decorative_retriever observed inertness and overlap on the natural pool, whereas here the property that would make the read non-inert is built in at two levels and confirmed on an independent draw.
Changes made:
- P3 (near_entailed): now a three-part claim about retriever and reader behaviour on the same bank: cross-type-in-top-3 and strict twin rates are logged per RET cell and a type-conditioned retrieval arm RET-T on N-48 is added; falsified if the retriever does not expose twins, if the reader ignores exposed twins (RET(N-48) flat against RET(R-48), reachable given blind1 is only 3 under k0), or if RET-T does not recover (item identity, not twins); the count-flatness part keeps its falsifier.
- P4 (entailed, headline): re-estimated as the route x composition interaction at matched length on an independent replicate draw (WB/RET on N'-80 and R'-80, disjoint items and combos), four cells used by no other prediction, with a bootstrap CI; the primary-draw interaction is exploratory; the falsifier (both routes lose the same to twins) is reachable because P3(a) now predicts retrieval is hurt too.
- P5 (unresolvable): both readers on the same 12/24/48/80 grid; estimand changed from a threshold crossover at the floor to the reader difference in D = [WB-RET](80) - [WB-RET](12) at the 9-net margin with a paired-bootstrap CI; crossing size is descriptive with a bootstrap CI, censored at above 80; the uninformative escape clause is removed, the 8B floor check is a precondition with Qwen3-14B as the pre-named fallback.
- P1, P2: one 9-net threshold for every contrast removes the 8-to-9 dead band; P2 is now contrasted at matched length (N-80 vs R-80) instead of against the S6 cell shared with P1, with the error-signature conjunct kept.
- P6: stated against Measurement C's measured k3 - static3 = +17.2 residual and made two-sided.
- Positive-control stop gate replaced by the finished Measurement C numbers (blind1 15.4 net below static3); the design proceeds without a stop.
- Budget: dropped F-24/F-48, R-24, RET S6 and the standalone order re-shuffle (absorbed by the replicate draw); added RET-T N-48, RET-rand N-48 and four replicate cells: 23 arms x 548 at 32B (about 35 GPU-h) plus 12 arms at 8B (about 6 GPU-h), about 20 h on two A100s.
- Sharpness kept: the central claim is unchanged and every prediction remains directional at a 9-net margin (whole-bank route flat under length and redundancy, declining with confusable count; retrieval exposure capped at k; interaction favours retrieval and grows for the weaker reader); no prediction was converted into a measurement, and the reader claim was made harder to pass (same grid, CI, no escape) rather than smaller.
